sub_sections.title: Project's pathways towards impact
sub_sections.content: MAESTRO delivers credible, traceable pathways from research outputs to the five expected impacts of call HORIZON-CL4-2026-05-DIGITAL-EMERGING-02. Against EI-01, three integrated research pillars advance AI agent model architecture, memory, and autonomous behaviour: the Neuro-Symbolic Planning and Reasoning Engine (WP2) produces D2-01 and D2-02, delivering formal sub-task graph decomposition and MCTS/HTN-LLM integration; the Adaptive Memory Architecture (WP3) produces D3-01 and D3-02, enabling coherent long-horizon agent behaviour; and Decentralised Multi-Agent Coordination (WP4, led by CERIA) produces D4-01 and D4-02, targeting coordination of ≥5 heterogeneous agents, ≥25% improvement in joint task completion over independent agent baselines, and formal proof of protocol convergence. Against EI-02, three sector demonstrators are deployed via EDIH networks and validated in Testing and Experiment Facilities: the Healthcare Demonstrator — Clinical Decision Support (WP5, led by NIHS) produces D5-02, achieving diagnostic reasoning accuracy within 10% of specialist clinician performance on a benchmark of 500 de-identified clinical cases spanning 5 diagnostic domains; the Manufacturing Demonstrator — Process Optimisation (WP6, led by ISIA) produces D6-02, demonstrating ≥15% defect reduction and ≥10% energy savings in a pilot factory; and the Logistics Transfer Demonstrator — Cross-Sector Generalisation (WP7, led by ELI) produces D7-02, targeting ≥20% improvement in disruption recovery time and ≥15% improvement in delivery schedule adherence, validated across 3 supply chain corridors. Against EI-03, MAESTRO strengthens European open strategic autonomy through a European-origin neuro-symbolic planning paradigm (D2-01, D2-02), formally verified coordination protocols submitted to ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 42 or IEEE (D4-03, M36), and the open-source MAESTRO framework (D9-02, M36) reducing European dependency on non-European AI agent platforms. Against EI-04, the MAESTRO benchmark suite (D8-03, M42) and open-source framework (D9-02) are contributed to the AI-on-demand platform, targeting adoption by ≥5 external research groups and ≥20 peer-reviewed publications in top AI venues. Against EI-05, MAESTRO addresses all three call-specified sectors: healthcare via WP5, advanced manufacturing via WP6, and in-vehicle autonomous driving via the architectural transferability mapping in D7-03 (M42). The open-source MAESTRO framework (WP9, led by BAL) targets ≥500 GitHub stars within 6 months of release, AI-on-demand platform contribution, validation through ≥2 TEFs, and technology transfer through ≥3 EDIHs. Key barriers include regulatory approval timelines for clinical AI tools under the EU AI Act, which are mitigated by NIHS's established HTA submission pathways and auditable reasoning traces built into the clinical demonstrator from project outset.

sub_sections.title: Measures to maximise impact — Dissemination, exploitation and communication
sub_sections.content: MAESTRO's dissemination, exploitation, and communication plan is structured around four target audiences and is an admissibility condition for this proposal. For the scientific community, ATU, CERIA, and BIIS will publish ≥20 peer-reviewed articles in top AI venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, AAMAS, AAAI) from M12 to M60, with all accepted manuscripts deposited in open repositories in alignment with Horizon Europe open access practices; the MAESTRO benchmark suite (D8-03, M42, led by FIIT) and framework modules will be contributed to the AI-on-demand platform by M42. For industry and SMEs, BAL leads WP9 (Dissemination, Exploitation and Communication), releasing the open-source MAESTRO framework (D9-02, M36) under a permissive licence, targeting ≥500 GitHub stars within 6 months of release, AI-on-demand platform contribution, validation through ≥2 TEFs, and technology transfer through ≥3 EDIHs; FIIT's EDIH network expertise supports dissemination workshops from M30, with ≥3 EDIHs actively disseminating MAESTRO technology by M48. For healthcare stakeholders, NIHS leads clinical dissemination, submitting the clinical validation report (D5-03, M42) to ≥1 national health technology assessment body and engaging ≥3 hospital networks in adoption planning by M48. For manufacturing, ISIA leads technology transfer to ≥5 manufacturing SMEs via the EIT Manufacturing network and EDIH partners by M48. Exploitation is differentiated by output type: core research outputs (neuro-symbolic planning engine, adaptive memory architecture, formally verified coordination protocols) will be assessed for patentability at M24 and M42 by consortium technology transfer offices; sector demonstrators are subject to joint ownership agreements with exploitation rights allocated by sector; and the open-source framework and benchmark suite are released under a permissive open-source licence. IPR is governed by the Consortium Agreement, covering background IP protection, foreground IP allocation, and access rights. Sustainability beyond the project is ensured through community-governed open-source stewardship (coordinator institution), EDIH network integration, commercial adoption pathways for the clinical and manufacturing demonstrators, and the standardisation submission to ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 42 or IEEE embedding MAESTRO coordination protocols in international standards. The project website (live by M3) and quarterly newsletters from M6 maintain public communication throughout the project lifetime. ELI leads logistics sector dissemination, with an integration roadmap for ELI operational systems by M48 and a cross-sector transferability mapping to in-vehicle autonomous driving completed by M42 (D7-03).
